newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BRAZIL MANAGER ZAGALLO ANSWERS CRITICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL MANAGER ZAGALLO ANSWERS CRITICS.

text.p: Brazil coach Mario Zagallo hit back at his detractors on Thursday, predicting that he would have the last laugh by leading his country to their fifth World Cup success next year.

"Sometimes criticism is made by people who have no right to make it. But I want them to carry on because it brings me luck. Let them continue because we are going to be five times champions with Za-ga-llo," he said, spelling out his name one syllable at a time.

Zagallo has received some vicious criticism for Brazil's performances in the Tournoi de France, even though they drew two games and won one, and the previous friendly away to Norway, which they lost 4-2.
Most of it has come from media based in Sao Paulo.
But the hard-headed 65-year-old, who won the World Cup as a player in 1958 and 1962, as a coach in 1970 and assistant coach in 1994, responded by reminding his critics of his curriculum.
The words "I'm four times world champion" passed his lips on at least half a dozen occasions and was familiar rhetoric from a man who has never been afraid to blow his own trumpet.
"I never lose my calm," he said. "If I did, I would not be four times winner of the World Cup."
"One person called me an old machine. He has no right to talk like that about someone who is victorious and has won four World Cups."
"If we win, win, win and still have people questioning us, you can only imagine what happens when we lose."
Brazil open their Copa America campaign on Friday with a group C game with Costa Rica only 72 hours after finishing their 1-0 win over England in the Tournoi de France.
Zagallo said he was delighted with the win against England. "It was a great performance in tactical terms," he said.
Brazil have won the Copa America, formerly known as the South American championship, four times, but always on home ground.

They are one of the few countries to have brought a full-strength squad because as world champions they are not involved in World Cup qualifying matches. This has made them favourites for a first triumph on foreign soil.
Brazil are expected to field an unchanged side from the one that started against England, apart from midfielder Denilson who was injured in Tuesday's game.
They beat Costa Rica in their last meeting in a friendly in 1992, when left-back Roberto Carlos was the only member of the current squad in the team.
